# phase-118 — Introspect the session: `:builtins`, `:modules` and `:prompt`

## Evidence — verified finding

```
Redblue can tell you which names are bound (`:vars`) but not what the language itself provides. src/repl/completer.rs completes against keywords, builtins and session bindings, so completion knows the answer and no command exposes it. Comparing against Ipp: `:builtins` and `:modules` are both present there and both absent here (REPL_AUDIT.md sections 2.2 and 2.5). A user cannot answer 'does this language have a regex module?' without leaving the REPL and reading src/stdlib.rs. `:prompt` is missing too, so the prompt string is not configurable - and it is currently a bug, since the banner advertises ':quit' while a bare quit is parsed as a program.
```

**Re-verify this before you change anything.** If the finding no longer
reproduces on `main`, stop and write that to `FINDINGS.md` — a stale phase must
never be "fixed" by inventing a change.

## Goal

Add `:builtins` listing every registered builtin with its module, `:modules` listing every module the runtime exposes, and `:prompt` showing or setting the prompt string. All three read from the same registry the completer already uses, so completion and introspection cannot drift apart - if they used separate lists, one would be wrong within a release. `:prompt` defaults to the string that currently works, and setting it must not affect parsing, only display.

## Definition of done

- [ ] `:builtins` lists every name in BUILTIN_NAMES and every one of them is callable in a following line
- [ ] `:modules` lists every entry in MODULES and every one of them resolves as a module
- [ ] the listing is derived from the same registry the tab completer uses - asserted by a test that compares the completer's name set to the command's output, so drift fails the gate rather than being noticed by a user
- [ ] `:prompt` prints the current prompt, and `:prompt <text>` changes it for subsequent lines only
- [ ] a prompt set to an empty string still parses input correctly and still evaluates a program
- [ ] a prompt containing `>>>` or other REPL-significant text does not break continuation or the numbered multi-line prompt
- [ ] `:builtins` and `:modules` produce deterministic ordering — asserted against two consecutive calls, because registry iteration order reaching output is a known defect class in this project
- [ ] edge_* cases cover an empty registry field, a prompt of only spaces, and a very long prompt that exceeds the terminal width
